series: Things Living In Your House, Part 9
sources: University of California IPM, Pest Notes: House Mouse (Publication 74106): mice squeeze through openings as small as 1/4 inch; can jump up to 12 inches from the floor onto a flat surface; females have 5-10 litters a year of about 5 or 6 pups; sexually mature 5-6 weeks after birth; do not need to drink water to survive if food supplies moisture; mostly nocturnal; gnaw electrical wires, gas lines, appliance cords and storage containers; seldom venture more than 30 feet from nest and food; can carry leptospirosis, salmonella and LCM virus; urine is a major allergen linked to early-onset asthma in sensitive children; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7483.html

Texas A&M AgriLife Extension, Rodents and Rodent Control (public health license course, 2024): house mouse leaves 50 to 75 droppings a day, droppings 1/8-1/4 inch with pointed ends; up to 3,000 urine microdroplets produced daily; many live outside during summer; https://extensionentomology.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2024/02/Rodents-and-rodent-control-public-health-license-course.pdf

title: One Mouse Leaves 75 Droppings a Day in Your Kitchen 🐭
tiktok_caption: one mouse can leave up to 75 droppings and 3,000 drops of pee a day 🐭 and the nest is probably close. Would you share your kitchen with one? 🧀 sure / 🪤 no way

beats.say: One mouse in your kitchen can leave up to seventy five droppings a day.
The house mouse. It comes out at night, while you sleep.
It gets in through a gap just a quarter of an inch wide.
And it can jump a foot straight up, right onto your counter.
It doesn't even need to drink. It gets its water from food.
Your food.
A female can have five to ten litters a year.
Five or six babies, every time.
And those babies can start having babies at about six weeks old.
In summer, lots of mice live outside, in gardens and fields.
Inside, they chew through wires, gas lines, and plastic containers.
And they rarely travel more than thirty feet from the nest.
Now the gross part. While a mouse explores, it doesn't hold it in.
One mouse can leave up to three thousand tiny drops of pee a day.
All over your counters and cupboards, in the dark.
Mouse pee is a major allergen. It's linked to asthma in some kids.
And mice can carry germs like salmonella.
Would you share your kitchen with one?
If you've seen one, its nest is probably closer than you think.
Follow me. Part ten is hiding in your closet.
